name: Kyoto
overview: Kyoto has enough beyond temples that visiting a handful of the standout ones makes sense — the top picks are each visually distinct rather than repetitive, so it doesn't feel like a checklist.

recommendations.title: Fushimi Inari Taisha
recommendations.summary: Thousands of vermilion torii gates up the mountainside. Absolute must.
recommendations.body: Thousands of vermilion torii gates up the mountainside, free, no closing time — great early morning before crowds. Unlike anything else on the trip.

recommendations.title: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
recommendations.summary: Gold-leaf building over a reflecting pond, very photogenic.
recommendations.body: Gold-leaf building over a reflecting pond, extremely photogenic, quick visit (about an hour).

recommendations.title: Kiyomizu-dera
recommendations.summary: Wooden hillside temple with a viewing stage, near historic streets.
recommendations.body: Wooden temple on a hillside with a large viewing stage, near the Higashiyama historic streets (Sannenzaka/Ninenzaka) — pairs naturally with wandering and shopping rather than being a standalone stop.

recommendations.title: Ginkaku-ji (Silver Pavilion) + Philosopher's Path
recommendations.summary: Optional 4th temple, quieter and less crowded.
recommendations.body: Quieter, less crowded than the other three — paired with the Philosopher's Path walk alongside it, a canal-side route lined with cherry trees (not blooming in February, but still a quiet forested walk).

recommendations.title: Kimono rental + historic streets walk
recommendations.summary: Hands-on traditional experience, paired with the Kiyomizu-dera walk.
recommendations.body: Kimono rental paired with walking the historic streets (Gion/Higashiyama) is probably the most efficient combo of the traditional-experience options — get the experience and a scenic backdrop in one go.

recommendations.title: Tea ceremony
recommendations.summary: Widely available, English-friendly options, about an hour.
recommendations.body: Widely available with many English-friendly options in the Gion/central area, usually about an hour — good if wanted in addition to the kimono/streets combo.

recommendations.title: Nishiki Market
recommendations.summary: Covered shopping street, lots of food stalls for grazing.
recommendations.body: Covered shopping street with lots of food stalls for grazing — scout vegetarian options ahead, some stalls are seafood/skewer-heavy.

recommendations.title: Pontocho Alley
recommendations.summary: Atmospheric riverside dining alley, more sit-down.
recommendations.body: Atmospheric riverside dining alley — more sit-down than Nishiki Market's grazing style.

recommendations.title: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
recommendations.summary: Nice-to-have, not a must; half-day add-on with Tenryu-ji.
recommendations.body: Nice-to-have rather than a must-do — slot as a half-day add-on paired with nearby Tenryu-ji temple grounds, not a full day.

recommendations.title: Fushimi Inari's mountain trail
recommendations.summary: The torii path continues up the mountain into genuine forest.
recommendations.body: Most visitors turn back after the first viewpoint, but the fuller hike moves into genuine forest and is much quieter than the crowded lower gates.

recommendations.title: Philosopher's Path
recommendations.body: A quiet forested canal-side walk near Ginkaku-ji, lined with cherry trees.

recommendations.title: Gion
recommendations.summary: Historic geisha district, good for an evening walk.
recommendations.body: Historic geisha district, good for an evening walk — possible geisha/maiko sightings near dusk around Hanamikoji-dori.
